2. The short facts giving leading to this rule are that Miscellaneous case No. 41 of 1981 was instituted under section 96(1) of State Acquistion and Tenancy Act, 1950 for pre-empting certain land in the court of Munsif, 4th Court Com ilia. The petitioner was impleaded in that preemption case as opposite party No. 11. The petitioner prayed for proportionate pre-emption of the land. The learned Munsif by an order dated 28.7.81 made him a co-applicant in that preemption case on establishment of a court of Munsif at Laksam the said case was transferred to that court and was re-numbered as Miscellaneous case No.1 38 of 1983. It was dismissed for default on 21.8.1984 but was restored to its file and number under Order 9, Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure by the learned Munsif on 6.11.1984 

 Mr. Mokbul Ahmed Chowdhury, the learned. Advocate for the petitioner challenged the propriety of the order complained of before me on the ground that the learned Munsif committed an error in law in passing the impugned order on an erroneous interpretation of law on the point. He submits that the petitioner having been impleaded as a co-applicant his right although was not existent on dismissal of the pre-emption case but it was revived with restoration of the said case with all its legal consequences. He further submits that section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act docs not require a co-applicant to deposit the required amount of money payable by him sou motu. Rather it is the duty of the court to determine the amount to be paid by each applicant and after such determination of the amount to pass an order for depositing the said amount by the applicant or the applicants within a reasonable period and only when an applicant fails to comply with the order of the Court his application for proportionate pre-emption is liable to be dismissed. Mr. Ahmed submits that no such order was passed by the court in the instant case. We place reliance upon section 96(6)(b) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950.
